#en: [This book just has lore and no actual functions]
zh: [本书仅有背景设定，没有实际功能]

#en: [The data slate contains information on a nearby mission]
zh: [该数据板包含附近任务的信息]

#en: The wreck came apart like rotten foil, but the black box did not. Its last seconds are clean, ordinary, then the course line bends a hair's breadth and everything tears loose. No interference spike, no pirate burn, just a neat little correction that should not exist. Listening to it on loop, I get the feeling the answer is right there in the numbers, as plain as basic nav, and somehow still refuses to resolve. All I really have is that lonely log from the edge of nowhere, a handful of "lucky" escapes, and a name nobody quite manages to say.
zh: 残骸像腐烂的锡箔一样裂开，但黑匣子没有。它记录的最后几秒干净、平常，随后航线弯了发丝般的一丝，一切便四分五裂。没有干扰尖峰，没有海盗的尾焰，只有一次本不该存在的小小修正。循环听着它，我总觉得答案就在那些数字里，像基础导航一样明白，却偏偏始终不肯成形。我真正拥有的，只有那段来自天涯尽头的孤独日志、几桩"幸运"的逃脱，以及一个谁都不太说得出口的名字。

#en:
I keep thinking how none of this would have happened if some UC clerk had just signed the right deorbit order.  
They left the station up here to save a little fuel and a little face, then cut maintenance hours, then reassigned anyone who remembered its passwords.  
One cheap decision at a time, until this place turned into a quiet pocket where a person could reroute half a dozen lanes and no one would notice.  

Now I sit in the dark, watching old dishes groan as they track something they are not supposed to see, replaying every "temporary" cost-cut and overlooked warning I have lived through.
zh:
我总在想，要是当初哪个联殖文员老老实实签了那份正确的脱轨指令，这一切都不会发生。
他们为了省一点燃料、保一点脸面，把这座空间站留在了上面，接着削减维护工时，再把所有还记得它密码的人调走。
一次一个便宜的决定，直到这地方变成一处安静的角落——有人可以在那里改掉半打航道而无人察觉。

如今我坐在黑暗里，看着老旧的天线呻吟着追踪它们不该看见的东西，一遍遍回想我亲历过的每一次"临时"削减与每一处被忽略的警告。

#en: I docked here because the tanks were low and the crew was tired, not because I believe in ghost currents and cursed lanes like the locals do. Then I pulled yesterday's nav dump and watched our course bend three degrees starboard without a single correction logged, same as the old timers swear it always does over that valley. The station master just shrugged and said some paths are easier not to question, especially when the cargo keeps moving and the bodies stay far enough away to forget. I do not know if I am more afraid of phantom gravity or the way everyone prefers the story that hurts them least.
zh: 我在这里停靠，只是因为燃料罐快空了、船员也累了，并不是像本地人那样相信什么幽灵洋流和被诅咒的航道。可后来我调出昨天的导航转储，眼看我们的航向无端向右偏了三度，日志里却没有一条修正记录——和那些老手赌咒说过的、在这片谷地上方一贯如此的情形一模一样。站长只是耸耸肩，说有些航道还是别追问为好，尤其是当货物照旧流通、尸体又远得足以让人忘掉的时候。我不知道自己更怕的是幽灵引力，还是人人都宁愿选择那个伤害自己最小的说法。

#en: I heard it from a dockhand who swore her cousin saw the account screens stutter right before the lights flickered, like the city took a breath and forgot who it owed. Nobody can show you a clean record, of course, just half-scorched dataslates and freight manifests with the same routes crossed out in different hands. Some say it is a GalBank ghost, some say it is pirates, some swear it is a woman from the lower decks of New Atlantis who knows exactly where the old wiring runs. All I know is whenever the rumors start, the people in suits suddenly talk quieter and the ones who live under the pipes listen harder.
zh: 我是从一名码头工那里听来的。她赌咒说她表亲亲眼看见账户屏幕在灯光闪烁前的一刹那卡了顿，就像这座城市喘了口气，忘了自己欠着谁。当然，谁也拿不出干净的记录，只有半焦的数据板和货运清单，上面同样的航线被不同人的笔迹划掉。有人说是银河银行的鬼，有人说是海盗，还有人发誓那是新亚特兰蒂斯下层甲板上的一个女人，她清楚那些旧线路究竟铺在哪里。我只知道，每当传言一起，穿西装的人说话就会忽然放轻，而住在管道下面的人则会听得更仔细。

#en: We were never meant to be out this far. Scarrunner was a hauler, not an explorer, but one little routing "optimization" slipped in during a maintenance cycle and nobody bothered to roll it back. Cheaper fuel, tighter jumps, the kind of thing captains brag about over drinks. Then the plotted paths started leaning, just a fraction, toward that junk-choked patch near the veil. Each run, same tiny adjustment, same quiet deviation that never tripped an alarm. Now I am floating in a dead ship, staring at logs that show how a minor tweak got copied, normalized, and finally steered us straight into the teeth of someone else's math.
zh: 我们本不该跑到这么远的地方。疤痕快船是艘货船，不是探险船，可是一次维护周期里溜进了小小的航路"优化"，谁也没费心把它回滚。燃料更省、跃迁更紧，正是船长们喝酒时会吹嘘的那种东西。而后标绘出的航线开始微微偏向帷幕附近那片塞满垃圾的区域，只偏那么一点点。每一趟都是同样的小调整，同样悄无声息的偏移，从未触发过一次警报。如今我漂在一艘死船里，盯着日志——上面显示一次微不足道的改动如何被复制、被规范化，最终把我们径直推进了别人算式里的獠牙。

#en: They say every tower in Neon has a ghost in the basement, but this one walks in numbers and routing codes instead of chains. I used to think the stories about vanished freighters and bought shortcuts were just bar noise that got louder on the way up the Span; now the whispers have paperwork behind them. Out on the fringe I tripped over a lone dataslate that should have been slagged, then heard a Ryujin clerk stammer through the same missing names, and finally cracked a cutter's half-burned logs that described the exact same kind of jump, like the rumor had learned how to write itself into every system that tried to erase it.
zh: 都说霓虹城每座塔楼的地下室里都有个鬼，可这一个是用数字和航路代码行走的，不是用锁链。我以前觉得那些关于失踪货船和买通捷径的故事，不过是酒吧里的噪声，越往跨桥上走越响；如今这些低语背后已经有了纸面记录。在外围区域，我绊到了一块本该被熔掉的孤立数据板，接着又听一名龙神文员结结巴巴地念出同样的失踪名字，最后撬开了一个切割工半烧毁的日志——里面描述着完全相同的那种跃迁，仿佛这则传言学会了把自己写进每一个试图抹去它的系统里。

#en: I heard the story before I ever set down here, but it was already worn smooth by the time it reached my ears. First it was a convoy that never checked in. Then it was "pirates," or "drive failure," or "bad coordinates in a storm." Ask three haulers at the bar and you get four versions, all of them saying less than they know. Out in the yard the cutters work overtime on incoming husks with scrubbed transponders, and nobody writes down who paid to bring them in. The earliest telling of what really happened has already drifted into speculation; all that is left are scared glances, half-finished sentences, and a feeling that someone is using the dark between the lanes as both grave and bank.
zh: 我还没在这里落脚就听过这个故事了，可等它传到我耳朵里时，早被磨得光滑圆润。起初是一支没能按时报到的运输队。然后是"海盗"，或是"引擎故障"，或是"风暴中的错误坐标"。在酒吧里随便问三个运货船员，你会得到四个版本，每一个都比他们知道的说得更少。外面的船坞里，切割工加班加点处理拖进来的船壳，应答器全被擦洗过，没人记下是谁出钱把它们弄来的。关于真相最早的讲述早已飘散成猜测；剩下的只有惊恐的目光、半截的话，以及一种感觉——有人在把航道之间的黑暗同时当作坟墓和银行。

#en: Funny how something that started as bar talk in The Well is now riding the lifts up into the nice parts of New Atlantis. I keep hearing the story come back to me in different mouths, polished a little more each time. A clerk swears they knew a hauler whose whole family license vanished between one shift and the next. A tech on a maintenance crew claims they heard a voice on a dormant line reciting case numbers that do not exist anymore. I saw the original slate that kicked this off, glitched timestamps and dead transponders, and I still do not know what scares me more now: that the story has outgrown whatever really happened, or that the truth is worse than the version people feel safe repeating.
zh: 说来好笑，一桩始于深井区酒吧闲谈的事，如今竟坐着电梯升进了新亚特兰蒂斯的上等街区。我不断听见这故事从不同的嘴里绕回到我这儿，每一次都被打磨得更光滑一点。一个文员赌咒说自己认识一名运货船员，那家人的整套执照在一个轮班与下一个轮班之间就消失了。一名维护班组的技工声称，自己在一段休眠线路上听到有声音背诵早已不存在的案号。我见过最初引爆这一切的那块数据板——时间戳错乱、应答器全死了——可如今我还是不知道哪个更让我害怕：是这故事已经长得比真正发生过的事还大，还是真相远比人们敢放心重复的那个版本更糟。

#en: They say every story up here has three versions the official one, the one told over drinks, and the one nobody says out loud. I have heard all three today and they do not even agree on the color of the sky. One UC patrol officer swore the distortion was a calibration fault, nothing more. A freighter hand in a smoke choked backroom swore on his last credits that something slid past his ship without a transponder, humming in his teeth like bad grav. And in the alley outside, a Neon runner laughed and said it was just an old test profile, long buried, nothing anyone should be asking about. Funny how everyone uses different words for the same thin slice of orbit, and how their voices all dip when they get to that part.
zh: 都说在上头，每个故事都有三个版本：官方的那一版、喝酒时讲的那一版，还有谁也不会说出口的那一版。今天我三个都听过了，它们连天空是什么颜色都对不上。一名联殖巡警赌咒说那处畸变只是校准故障，仅此而已。一名货船船员在烟雾弥漫的后室里，拿他最后几个信用币起誓，说有东西没开应答器就从他船边滑了过去，像糟糕的重力一样在他牙缝里嗡鸣。而外面巷子里，一个霓虹城的跑腿笑着说是那只是老旧的测试剖面，早就埋掉了，谁都不该去打听。好笑的是，大家对同一小片轨道用着各不相同的说法，而讲到那一段时，所有人的声音都会往下沉。

#en: I always trusted GalBank lanes. You fly the blue logo, you assume someone in a clean shirt and better pay has triple-checked the math. Maybe that is how they got away with it. We ran that corridor so often I could draw the buoy pattern from memory, right down to the little skip where the grav well makes your teeth hum. When the escort failed to report in, nobody flinched; consoles shrugged, called it a relay glitch, filed another green stamp. It took three missed convoys and one freighter limping back with its drive casing warped before anyone bothered to pull the raw logs. That is when we saw the extra projections tucked between routine updates, pointing toward a skinny band of rock and ice that was never on any of our official charts.
zh: 我一向信赖银河银行的航道。你飞着那个蓝色标志，就默认某个衬衫干净、薪水更高的人已经把算式核对过三遍。也许他们就是靠这个得手的。我们跑那条走廊跑得太勤，闭着眼都能画出浮标排布，连重力井让你牙齿发麻的那个小小顿挫都记得一清二楚。护航队没能按时报到时，没人惊慌；控制台只是耸耸肩，称之为中继站故障，又盖了一枚绿章。直到三支运输队失踪、一艘货船驱动外壳扭曲着跛行归来，才有人肯去调原始日志。就是在那里，我们看见例行更新之间夹着额外的投影，指向一条从未出现在任何官方星图上的细长岩冰带。

#en:
I keep replaying the approach in my head, but every time it runs a little different.  
The telemetry said clear lane, clean gravity, no debris worth naming, and still the hauler ahead of us drifted off-course like something was tugging at its teeth.  
We scooped three escape pods; the black took the rest.  
LIST stamped it down as pilot error, Argos called the basin a bad investment, and the official records all agree it was nobody's fault in particular.  
Only the stories in station bars refuse to line up, little fragments about the same burned pads, the same families, the same quiet pilot who swore the numbers were solid.  
Some days I think I imagined that extra ping on the scope; other days I am sure it was a hand on the wheel that never makes it into the logs.
zh:
我在脑子里一遍遍重放那次进近，可每次跑起来都略有不同。
遥测显示航道通畅、重力干净、没有值得命名的碎片，可我们前方那艘货船还是偏了航，像有什么在拽它的牙齿。
我们捞起三个逃生舱；其余的都被黑暗收走了。
独立盟把它归为驾驶员失误，阿戈斯称那片盆地是笔糟糕的投资，官方记录也一致认定这不特别怪谁。
只有空间站酒吧里的故事死活对不上：一些碎片般的说法，讲着同样的焦黑停机坪、同样的家庭、同样那个赌咒数据可靠、沉默寡言的飞行员。
有些日子我觉得雷达上那道多余的信号是我自己想象出来的；另一些日子我又确信，那是某只握在操纵杆上的手——而它永远不会出现在日志里。

#en: I log beacon checks at the start and end of every shift. Always have. Flip through the same diagnostics, tap the same acknowledgements, watch the same green lights blink in the same order. Somewhere in the last year, that order changed and I did not see it. A handoff here took a heartbeat longer, a timestamp there drifted by a fraction. The system compensated, captains cursed their nav suites, and traffic flowed on. Only now, looking back over old traces, do I see how the routes bent, almost politely, around the same handful of worlds. The frozen outpost that did not get its evac, the survey run nobody could re-plot, the approvals a LIST clerk swears they sent. The pattern was there the whole time, threaded through my consoles like a quiet apology I never bothered to read.
zh: 我在每个轮班的开始和结束都会记录信标检查。一向如此。翻过同样的诊断项，点下同样的确认，看着同样的绿灯以同样的顺序闪烁。可就在过去这一年里的某个时候，那个顺序变了，而我没看出来。这里一次交接多花了半拍心跳，那里一个时间戳漂移了一丝。系统自行补偿了，船长们咒骂着他们的导航套件，交通照常流动。直到现在，回头翻看旧的轨迹，我才看清那些航线是如何几乎彬彬有礼地绕开同样那几颗星球。那座没等到撤离的冰封哨站、那次谁都重绘不出的勘测航行、那份独立盟文员赌咒说已经发出的批文。图案一直都在，像一句安静的道白穿过我的控制台——而我从未费心去读。

#en: I am recording this from a rented bunk bolted to bulkhead C, because if I say it out loud in the bar again it will turn into another story and I need it to stay a fact.\n\nThe TA broker here swears the manifests he showed me are just misfiled freight, nothing to see, just frontier bookkeeping. But his hands shook when he scrolled past the third ship with the same registry, three different captains, three different lien codes. Same audit signature on each. He told me, real soft, that if I wanted the rest of that pattern I should go where the metal and the money meet: the yards in Gagarin, where freighters are reborn with new names and old debts. Everyone else talks about a ghost auditor like a campfire tale, changing details each time, but her accent and those codes never change.
zh: 我从一张用螺栓固定在 C 隔舱上的租用铺位上录下这段话，因为要是我再在酒吧里大声讲出来，它就会变成又一个故事，而我需要它保持为一个事实。\n\n这里的贸易管理局经纪商赌咒说他给我看的那些清单只是归错了档的货物，没什么可看的，不过是边地记账罢了。可当他滑过第三艘登记号相同的飞船时，他的手在抖——三个不同的船长，三个不同的扣押代码。每一份上都是同样的审计签名。他压低声音告诉我，要是我想看到那图案的其余部分，就该去金属与金钱交汇的地方：加加林的船坞，那里的货船会以新名字和旧债务重生。别的人都把那位幽灵审计员当成篝火边的故事来讲，每次细节都不同，可她的口音和那些代码从来不变。

#en: I have been sleeping next to the bunker wall, just to feel the hum through the metal. It is thin, a background tremor in the old UC wiring, but it matches the cadence I saw in the patrol logs I stole. Same gaps. Same timing. She is still riding the grid.\n\nNo one back at New Atlantis wanted to see it. They skimmed my report once, then started staring past my shoulder, like I was a static burst they could tune out. Out here, the bunker still listens to a sky the registry pretends is quiet, and tonight I caught something new: a tight-beam exchange, bouncing through an unlisted node, then vanishing toward that cluster of grav scars the Crimson crews call the blind corridor. Whatever she is doing next, she is staging it off a dead relay, just far enough outside the charts that no one has to admit it exists.
zh: 我近来一直睡在碉堡墙边，就为了透过金属感受那阵嗡鸣。它很细微，是联殖老线路里的一段背景震颤，可它与我偷来的巡逻日志里看到的节律吻合。同样的间隔。同样的时间。她还在骑着那张电网。\n\n新亚特兰蒂斯那边没人愿意承认它。他们只把我的报告扫了一眼，然后就盯着我肩膀后面的空气，仿佛我只是段能被调静音的静电爆音。而在这外面，碉堡仍在倾听着星图声称寂静的天空，今晚我逮到了新东西：一次窄束通讯，经一座未列名的节点弹跳，随后朝着深红舰队那帮人称作"盲廊"的那簇重力伤痕消失。无论她下一步要做什么，她都在借一座死中继站来布场——远在星图之外，远到没人非得承认它存在。

#en: I keep telling myself I am just here to clean up a mess in the logs, but the deeper I dig, the less it looks like random corruption. The theft chain they handed me was supposed to be simple follow the unauthorized copies, close the holes, file the report. Instead I am staring at the same warped jump curves cropping up in places that should never share traffic, tagged with user IDs that do not exist in any personnel registry I can see. One of the senior analysts flagged this pattern weeks ago, left a half-finished trace on their console, then took urgent leave and never came back to finish what they started. Tonight I pushed their old trace one step further and found a match buried in offsite telemetry from a navy hull that should be nowhere near these experiments, let alone echoing the same impossible vectors.
zh: 我不断告诉自己，我来这里只是清理日志里的一团乱麻，可我挖得越深，它就越不像随机的损坏。他们交给我的这条盗窃链本该很简单：顺着未授权的副本追下去，堵住漏洞，提交报告。可我却盯着同样扭曲的跃迁曲线在意想不到的地方冒出来——那些地方本不该共享任何交通——还带着我看遍所有人员登记册都查不到的用户 ID。有位资深分析师几周前就标记过这个图案，在控制台上留下一段没做完的追踪，随后请了紧急事假，再没回来把自己开头的活儿做完。今晚我把他那段旧追踪又往前推了一步，在来自一具海军船体的站外遥测里找到了一处匹配——那艘船本不该靠近这些实验，更别说回响出同样不可能的矢量。
